questions.question: Which of the following is one of the strengths of cross-sectional study?
questions.correct_answer: B. suggests association between exposure and disease
wrong_answers: D. Free of different types of bias

questions.question: A surgeon reports outcomes on 10 patients who underwent a new procedure without a comparison group. What is this study design?
You want to measure current prevalence of anaemia among pregnant women attending antenatal care clinics. Which study design best fulfill your objective?
A cross-sectional study is also known as which of the following?
A researcher studies per-capita cigarettes sales and heart disease rates across different countries. What is this design?
Estimating the prevalence of obesity in school children in relation to sex is an example of which of the following studies?
Ecological studies are NOT used for which of the following purposes?
wrong_answers: B. Correlate between two quantitative variables.
C. Determining the contextual effect of risk factors on the population.
D. Determining the effect of a risk factor and disease occurrence on the individual level

questions.question: An investigator screened 1000 women above 50 years of age using mammography to sort out those with cancer breast from those without. He also asked about current use of oral contraceptive pills intake. What type of study designs was this?
Five children with hepatoblastoma (rare form of cancer liver) were reported. History showed past exposure to a specific insecticide. What is the type of this study design?

In 2024, researchers measured body mass index (BMI) and physical activity levels among office employees at the same point in time. They assessed the association between physical inactivity and obesity. Which type of study design best describes this investigation?
Which of the following is a key characteristic of cross-sectional studies?
questions.correct_answer: B. The research can collect many variables at the same time.
wrong_answers: A. It involves an intervention that the researcher applies.
C. Test hypothesis about cause effect relationship
D. Deal with average population data

questions.question: What is the main feature of the cross-sectional study design?
questions.correct_answer: C. It measures the exposure & outcome simultaneously in a population at a specific point in time.
wrong_answers: A. Subjects are followed over a long period of time.
B. It compares two groups: subjects with a disease to subjects without the disease.
D. It is the only design that establishes a cause-and-effect relationship

questions.question: Which of the following statements characterizes case report?
wrong_answers: B. Can measure prevalence of disease.
C. Can measure the efficacy of certain treatments.
D. Can measure incidence of disease

questions.question: What is the epidemiological study design that measures the association between two different quantitative variables?

Researchers want to investigate the relationship between smoking status and chronic respiratory disease among adults in a city. They select 1,000 adults and assess both smoking habits and lung function on the same day. What is the type of this epidemiological study design?
Case report and case series are both important in which of the following?
questions.correct_answer: C. Identifying new clinical features of a known disease.
wrong_answers: A. Measuring prevalence of a disease.
B. Measuring incidence of a disease.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of a cross-sectional study?
questions.correct_answer: B. Can measure prevalence in a population
wrong_answers: A. Can determine temporality between exposure and disease

questions.question: A study that compares disease rates and exposures across different populations or communities, rather than individuals, what is the name of this study?
Which of the following is an advantage of correlation study?
wrong_answers: B. Data are available on the individual level
D. The risk of exposure is calculated

questions.question: In a review of health data, researchers find that communities with higher levels of physical activity report lower rates of obesity. They conclude that all individuals in these communities have a lower risk of being obese due to higher levels of physical activity. What type of bias does this conclusion exhibit?
Which of the following best defines a confounding factor?
questions.correct_answer: B. A variable related to both exposure and outcome and distorts the association
wrong_answers: A. A variable that lies on the causal pathway between exposure and outcome
C. A variable that occurs after the outcome and cannot influence the relationship
D. A variable that is unrelated to both the exposure and the outcome

questions.question: What is the study in which the units of observation are populations or groups of people rather than individuals?
An investigator collected data on infant mortality rates in different governorates of Egypt and the average family size in these governorates in the year 2005. What is the type of the design?
Which of the following is a key limitation of cross-sectional studies?
Which of the following statements correctly describes descriptive studies?
questions.correct_answer: C. They identify patterns of disease and generate hypotheses
wrong_answers: A. They are designed to establish causal relationships
B. They always include a control or comparison group
D. They have limited usefulness for public health planning

questions.question: A researcher studied the relation between vaccination coverage rate of BCG vaccine in different countries and the average incidence rate of COVID 19. What is this type of study?
Which of the followings is considered an advantage(s) of cross-sectional study?
questions.correct_answer: B. Quick, easy, needs minimal resources
wrong_answers: A. Can prove a relation between an exposure and an outcome
C. Can estimate the risk (incidence) of developing a disease in a community
D. Suitable for studying acute and fatal diseases

questions.question: What is the main limitation of a case report?
wrong_answers: A. It is expensive and time-consuming
C. It requires large sample sizes

questions.question: A research team wished to investigate a possible association between tobacco use and oral lesions among a group of workers. At periodic employment examination, each worker was asked about tobacco use, and a dentist examined them for the presence of oral lesion. What is the type of the study design?

During pre-placement examination of 200 new employees, 20 persons were hypertensive among 80 smokers, while 6 hypertensive persons were detected among the remaining 120 non-smokers, What is the prevalence of hypertension among smokers in this study?

A large, multi-country study is conducted to determine the effect of economic development on cancer incidence and mortality. The study uses data obtained from the national cancer registries, along with information regarding per capita gross domestic product as reported by the international Monetary Fund and life expectancy as reported by the World Health Organization. Which of the following best describes the design of this study?

A study is designed to describe the manifestations of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) on imaging studies, particularly on computerized tomography (CT) scans. Eleven patients with COVID-19 are recruited for the study and their CT findings are studied and characterized. Which of the following best describes this study design?

Researchers are studying the relationship between essential hypertension and a common mutation in the structure of a sodium channel protein. A study population is randomly selected and blood samples are obtained for leukocyte genotyping. The prevalence of hypertension is determined based on mean blood pressure measurements obtained using standardized ambulatory blood pressure monitoring conducted over 1 week. Based on the analysis results, the researchers conclude that the sodium channel structure mutation is associated with hypertension. Which of the following best describes the study design used by the investigators?

Researchers want to explore the association between selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) use and pulmonary tuberculosis. A random sample of subjects age 20-84 with newly diagnosed pulmonary tuberculosis and an independent random sample of subjects without pulmonary tuberculosis are enrolled in the study. Subsequently, subjects who never had a prescription for an SSRI are defined as "never users," and those who have had a prescription for an SSRI are defined as "users" The study compares the frequency of SSRI use in subjects with and without a diagnosis of pulmonary tuberculosis and determines that SSRI use with pulmonary tuberculosis. Which of the following best describes the design of this study?

A 73-year-old man has stable Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL). A new drug prolongs survival but does not cure the disease. If this drug is widely used, what happens to incidence and prevalence of CLL?
questions.correct_answer: C. The number of incident cases will not change, the number of prevalent cases will increase
wrong_answers: A. The number of incident cases will increase, the number of prevalent cases will not change
B. The number of incident cases will decrease, the number of prevalent cases will increase
D. The number of incident cases will not change, the number of prevalent cases will not change

questions.question: The prevalence of a chronic disease that affects mostly older individuals has been constant in a population for the last 15 years. As a result of worsening economic conditions that have no effect on the disease itself, many young healthy individuals emigrate from the population. Which of the following is the most likely effect of the emigration on the estimate of disease prevalence over the next few years?
wrong_answers: C. The prevalence would remain the same
D. It is not possible to determine the effect on prevalence from the information given

questions.question: Ecologic fallacy refers to:
questions.correct_answer: C. Ascribing the characteristics of a group to every individual in that group
wrong_answers: A. Assessing exposure in large groups rather than in many small groups
B. Assessing outcome in large groups rather than in many small groups
D. Examining correlations of exposure and outcomes rather than timetrends

questions.question: Residents of three villages with three different types of water supply were asked to participate in a survey to identify cholera carriers. Because several cholera deaths had occurred recently, virtually everyone present at the time underwent examination. The proportion of residents in each village who were carriers was computed and compared. What is the proper classification for this study?
